title: Safe ECR repository operation
summary: Test publisher, consumer and unapproved access; separate repository authorization from identity-policy authentication. Preview expiry by digest and protect still-needed versions by excluding them from eligibility.

blocks.text: An ECR repository policy grants specified principals operations such as image pulls or image-layer uploads.
Scope principals and actions to approved publishers and consumers; test push, pull and an unapproved principal.
Authentication also needs ecr:GetAuthorizationToken through an identity policy. Repository permissions alone do not grant that action.

Compare the publisher’s push, consumer’s pull and unapproved principal’s test. Authentication and repository authorization are separate: an authenticated principal still needs the relevant repository grant.

blocks.takeaway: Authentication and repository authorization need separate evidence.

public.prompt: A principal has repository pull permissions but no identity-policy authorization for ecr:GetAuthorizationToken. What does the repository policy alone establish?

options.text: Repository pull permission, not authorization for the authentication action.
Authorization for ecr:GetAuthorizationToken as well as pull.
Authentication is unnecessary whenever repository pull is granted.

o3.message: Not supported. ECR authentication requires ecr:GetAuthorizationToken through an identity policy.

blocks.text: ECR lifecycle policies expire images selected by criteria such as tag status and count or age.
Express supplied retention using rulePriority, selection and action. Run a lifecycle preview before applying it.
Compare previewed digests with deployed versions. Exclude still-needed versions from eligible expiry; deployment does not make images immune.

Use the preview table to compare eligible digests with deployed and still-needed flags. If a needed digest would expire, revise eligibility before applying the policy; a deployment reference is not protection.

segments.label: Preview and apply count-based ECR lifecycle rules
segments.summary: ECR lifecycle policies can clean up older images while retaining recent versions. This example starts in the lifecycle-rule preview tab and sets rule priorities, tag prefixes and image-count thresholds for tagged images. It also adds a separate rule selecting untagged images above a count threshold. After reviewing the result, the policy is applied. These counts illustrate the creator's repository needs; use the supplied approved criteria for your own retention decision.

bridge.before: Watch how tag prefixes, tag status and image counts define eligibility. The clip calls lifecycle preview a “dry run”; its example counts are not your approved retention criteria.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates count-based selection and application, but not the complete rulePriority, selection and action structure or deployed-digest checks. The text supplies both; deployment does not protect an eligible image.
